comparator.name: Middle Eastern Studies
comparator.route: Modern Middle East Studies with Arabic
comparator.sourceNotes: The current Modern Middle East Studies catalogue provides 60 EC in year one and 60 EC in year two. It labels year three 60 EC but lists History of Central Asia & Afghanistan in both compulsory year-two and year-three blocks. The 5 EC module appears once in the 175 EC inventory. The formal 2026 regulations identify the broad regional direction, and the course guide supplies the individual modules. The 25 EC Arabic language and project sequence follows preparatory script study. The second Arabic course and the language project follow Arabic 1. Comparative literatures requires the first-year diploma. The thesis seminar and thesis normally require year one and 55 EC of year two. The 30 EC elective block is separate. No replacement has been confirmed for the duplicated module.

exception.ucrCourseEvidence: The active workbook supports some regional examples and broader historical, political, legal, economic and qualitative methods. A feasible internal course proposal tests that combination. Full comparability depends on confirmation of the external programme structure.

candidateAssessment.concept: Comparative regional history, politics and political economy
candidateAssessment.assessment: A feasible 180 EC proposal has foundations in history, economics and law and advances to political inquiry, historical methods and political economy. Its sustained subject matter is comparative or centres other regions. Selected Middle Eastern materials establish a real connection without confirming a comparable regional pathway. Final judgment awaits external confirmation.

candidateAssessment.concept: Middle Eastern cultures, languages and religions
candidateAssessment.assessment: World Myth & Literature uses Arabic and Near Eastern materials, and Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean explicitly includes Islamic courts. Archaeology and comparative cultural methods provide context. Available courses do not supply a sustained language, literature or religious studies sequence for the region. Final judgment awaits external confirmation.
